help.step.label: Step {n} of {total}
help.system.intro.body.1: You can walk through every step from System to Export once, without a mic or REW.
help.system.intro.body.2: The tutorial opens a separate project of the demo room (7.1.4 · 3 subs). Your project stays as it is, and you return to it when the tutorial ends.
help.system.intro.body.3: During the tutorial the accent color turns magenta and the rail shows 'Tutorial'. Measuring is simulated, so nothing plays, and the project cannot be saved or exported.
help.system.intro.body.4: You do not need REW Pro. Measure with built-in measurement, or import mdat files measured in REW in Measure & import. Automatic measuring through REW needs REW Pro in API mode.
help.system.intro.route.1: System: the demo room setup and the 'Main seat' arrangement are filled in.
help.system.intro.route.2: Connect & check: the measurement method is simulated measurement. Press 'Check all channel levels'.
help.system.intro.route.3: Measure & import: press 'Load demo data' to fill position 1.
help.system.intro.route.4: Correction: press 'Calculate correction', then go through the SPL, GD, XO and BA tabs.
help.system.intro.route.5: Export: the tutorial saves no files. In a real project this step exports the CamillaDSP configuration and REW mdat files.
help.system.intro.route.6: End: 'End tutorial' in the tutorial list returns to your project.
help.system.intro.outro.1: Press F1 on any step to open its help. The screen stays usable while help is open.
help.system.steps.goal: Record which speaker is connected to which output, and decide how many positions to measure. The measuring order and the export channels follow the output patch.
help.system.steps.1.do: Under Setup, pick the preset that matches the room.
help.system.steps.1.see: The output patch fills with one row per speaker. 7.1.4 has 12 rows; the demo room has two more subs, so 14.
help.system.steps.2.see: Each sub adds or removes a row in the output patch. You can have 0–8 subs.
help.system.steps.3.do: If a speaker is missing, press 'Add speaker'.
help.system.steps.3.see: A new row appears at the bottom of the output patch. Remove rows you do not need with 'Remove' at the end of the row.
help.system.steps.4.do: Match each row's measurement output to the real wiring.
help.system.steps.4.see: A duplicate number, or one beyond the device's outputs, is marked in its cell and listed below the output patch.
help.system.steps.5.see: Set polarity to Inverted only for speakers wired in reverse. Size can stay as the preset set it: Small applies the crossover, Large plays full range.
help.system.steps.6.do: Under Export DSP, pick your DSP device.
help.system.steps.6.see: The filter resources change to that device's values. The FIR budget feeds the FIR budget warning in Correction and the MIMO FIR support budget. Editing a value switches the device to Custom.
help.system.steps.7.do: Under Measurement arrangement, pick the one that fits where you listen.
help.system.steps.7.see: 'Main seat' (1 position) is for a quick check. For a single chair, pick 'One chair' (9 positions); for a sofa, pick 'Sofa for 2–3' (13) or 'Two rows' (17).
help.system.steps.8.see: Position 1 is the listening position and the reference for level and delay alignment. Half-filled markers are positions with the mic 20 cm higher or lower.
help.system.steps.9.do: Check the timing reference and the reference speaker.
help.system.steps.9.see: Keep the default, 'Acoustic · reference speaker'. The reference speaker cannot be a sub.
help.system.steps.10.see: It shows the time per position and the total. Moving the mic is not included.
help.system.steps.11.do: Press 'Go to Connect & check' in the step header.
help.system.steps.11.see: Connect & check opens. Press System in the rail to come back here.
help.system.checks.1: The measurement output is the output number of the audio device the sweep plays from. Patch the DSP inputs by the same numbers.
help.system.checks.2: Changing the preset, the sub count or the arrangement clears existing measurements. With measurements present, a confirmation opens first, and the notification after the change can undo it.
help.system.checks.3: Keep positions at least 30 cm apart and the whole spread at least 1 m across.
help.system.checks.4: Spread the height too, ear height ±20 cm.
help.system.checks.5: For real use, measure at least 5 positions. MIMO needs 3 positions or more.
help.system.checks.6: With the timing reference set to 'None', distance, delay and BA cannot be calculated.
help.system.trouble.1.symptom: 'Go to Connect & check' cannot be pressed.
help.system.trouble.1.fix: The reason shows in the step header. Usually two rows share an output, or a speaker has none. 'Renumber outputs' fixes duplicate numbers.
help.system.trouble.2.symptom: The measurement output device shows no channel count.
help.system.trouble.2.fix: Choose the measurement output device in Connect & check. Its channel count appears once it is chosen.
help.system.trouble.3.symptom: The time estimate is too long.
help.system.trouble.3.fix: Pick an arrangement with fewer positions, or shorten the sweep under Connect & check. Shorter sweeps pick up more noise.
help.system.trouble.4.symptom: The speaker you want is not in the reference list.
help.system.trouble.4.fix: The list follows the speakers in the output patch. A sub cannot be the reference speaker.
help.system.trouble.5.symptom: Timing looks wrong with the loopback reference.
help.system.trouble.5.fix: Connect a spare output to a spare input with a cable. Choose the loopback input channel in Connect & check; when measuring with REW, set the reference input in REW as well.
help.system.real.1: The audio interface and the DSP must be wired by the output patch's numbers. A wrong number plays a different speaker.
help.system.real.2: 'Save output patch as CSV' saves the table for patching the DSP inputs.
help.system.real.3: Enter your device's FIR taps and FIR budget under Export DSP. Correction then warns about results that do not fit that device.
help.system.real.4: In practice you move the mic for every position. A start delay gives you time to step away after pressing 'Measure this position'.
help.system.real.5: With the acoustic timing reference, the reference speaker plays a short reference signal before every sweep. The extra sound is expected.
help.system.real.6: Adding a few points 20–30 cm outside the sofa prevents overcorrection.
help.connect.steps.goal: Choose the measurement method, check the devices and the mic, then set the mic level for every channel. When you only import mdat files measured in REW, this step is skipped.
help.connect.steps.1.see: Built-in measurement plays and records the sweeps through your audio devices. REW drives REW Pro remotely in API mode. Simulated measurement plays nothing and uses responses measured in the demo room. 'Import mdat files only' skips this step.
help.connect.steps.2.do: With REW, press 'Start REW in API mode'.
help.connect.steps.2.see: If REW is not running, it starts (10–20 s). Continue when the state reads 'API connected · 127.0.0.1:4735'. If REW is already running, press 'Check again'.
help.connect.steps.3.see: With Pro confirmed, this app runs the sweeps through REW. Without Pro, measure in REW yourself and import the mdat files.
help.connect.steps.4.do: Set the input device and input channel to the measurement mic.
help.connect.steps.4.see: Built-in measurement lists the system's devices; REW lists its own. The mic's name should appear.
help.connect.steps.5.do: Check the output device, the mic calibration file and the sweep length.
help.connect.steps.5.see: The output device is the measurement output device used in System. Keep the sweep length at the default 256k (about 5.5 s).
help.connect.steps.6.do: Place the mic at ear height at the listening position and start with the master output low.
help.connect.steps.6.see: Start quiet and raise the level step by step.
help.connect.steps.7.do: Press play on the first channel.
help.connect.steps.7.see: It plays for 2.5 s: a 50 Hz sine on subs, pink noise on the others. The meter should land in the recommended range (−30…−15 dBFS).
help.connect.steps.8.do: If the meter is below or above the recommended range, adjust the master output and play again.
help.connect.steps.8.see: The current level (dBFS) shows at the end of the row.
help.connect.steps.9.do: Press 'Check all channel levels' in the step header.
help.connect.steps.9.see: The channels play in turn and their values fill in. When every channel has a level, Connect & check is marked done in the rail.
help.connect.checks.1: REW must run with the -api option. REW started without it does not connect.
help.connect.checks.2: Make sure the input channel is the one the mic is plugged into. Otherwise the level meter does not move.
help.connect.checks.3: Check that every channel lands in the recommended range. If one channel is far lower, check its wiring and amplifier first.
help.connect.checks.4: REW output above −6 dBFS must be unlocked in REW. Start low to protect the speakers.
help.connect.checks.5: Change the mic gain on the audio device or in REW, not in this app.
help.connect.checks.6: 'Fill with defaults' fills every channel with a level inside the recommended range. Use it only to see the flow.
help.connect.trouble.1.fix: If REW runs without -api, close it and press 'Start REW in API mode' again. Once the REW window is open, press 'Check again'.
help.connect.trouble.2.symptom: The input device list is empty.
help.connect.trouble.2.fix: With REW, press 'Check again' after REW connects to read the list again. With built-in measurement, the list fills again when the device is plugged in.
help.connect.trouble.3.symptom: 'A REW Pro license is required' appears.
help.connect.trouble.3.fix: REW cannot measure automatically. Switch the measurement method to built-in measurement, or import mdat files measured in REW in Measure & import.
help.connect.trouble.4.fix: REW did not report that value. Check it in REW itself.
help.connect.trouble.5.symptom: The level meter does not move at all.
help.connect.trouble.5.fix: Check that the input device and input channel match the mic.
help.connect.trouble.6.fix: Compare the channel's measurement output in System with the real wiring.
help.connect.trouble.7.symptom: The meter goes above the recommended range.
help.connect.trouble.7.fix: Lower the master output. Too high a level can clip the sweep.
help.connect.trouble.8.symptom: The device refuses the chosen sharing mode.
help.connect.trouble.8.fix: On Windows, a device can refuse a sharing mode fixed to Exclusive or Shared. Set the sharing mode to Automatic.
help.connect.real.1: To measure with REW, start it first as roomeqwizard.exe -api.
help.connect.real.2: This app runs sweeps through REW only with a REW Pro license. Without one, use built-in measurement, or measure in REW and import the mdat files.
help.connect.real.3: With REW, the input device, channel and mic calibration file are read from REW's settings. If REW uses a different calibration file per input, this screen cannot show it.
help.connect.real.4: The level check plays pink noise, and a 50 Hz sine on subs. Keep the room quiet so the values stay steady.
help.connect.real.5: When the level check ends, the recommended sweep level is stored in the measurement settings and the sweeps in Measure & import play at that level.
help.connect.real.6: Simulated measurement plays nothing and uses responses measured in the demo room. Use it to learn the flow.
help.measure.steps.goal: Place the mic where the map shows and measure every channel at each position. You can also import mdat files measured in REW.
help.measure.steps.1.do: Look at 'Position k / N' and the map.
help.measure.steps.1.see: The position to measure next is shown in the accent color on the map. You can also pick it in the position list.
help.measure.steps.2.do: Put the mic there and press 'Measure this position' in the step header.
help.measure.steps.2.see: Each channel sweeps in turn. If the project has never been saved, a window to choose where to save it opens first.
help.measure.steps.3.see: The job tray shows progress, elapsed and remaining time. To stop, press 'Cancel measurement' or 'Cancel' in the job tray.
help.measure.steps.4.do: Look at the graph and the position list.
help.measure.steps.4.see: The graph draws the channel curves, and the position turns 'Measured' in the list.
help.measure.steps.5.do: If more positions remain, move the mic and press 'Measure this position' again.
help.measure.steps.5.see: After each position, the next one is selected.
help.measure.steps.6.do: Check that every position is measured.
help.measure.steps.6.see: 'All positions measured (N)' appears and Measure & import is marked done in the rail.
help.measure.steps.7.do: If you measured in REW, press 'Import mdat'.
help.measure.steps.7.see: After you pick a file, a window opens to assign a channel and position to each measurement. Check the values filled in from the names and press 'Import measurements (N)'. The 'mdat import' tab has the details.
help.measure.checks.1: Measuring needs a saved project. For a new project that was never saved, a window to choose its location opens before measuring.
help.measure.checks.2: To redo a suspicious position, select it in the list and measure it again. Only that position's measurements change.
help.measure.checks.3: If a warning says the signal-to-noise ratio is below 20 dB, raise the level or use a longer sweep.
help.measure.checks.4: The position cannot change while measuring.
help.measure.checks.5: With the acoustic timing reference, sweep repeats are fixed at 1.
help.measure.checks.6: You can save one mdat file per position and import each. Add _P2 to the names of position 2's measurements. Example: L_P2
help.measure.trouble.1.fix: Look for a signal-to-noise warning. Raise the level or lengthen the sweep under Connect & check.
help.measure.trouble.2.symptom: One channel's curve is far lower.
help.measure.trouble.2.fix: Check its output number under System and the wiring. Measure the position again after fixing it.
help.measure.trouble.3.symptom: The last position was measured wrong.
help.measure.trouble.3.fix: Clear it with 'Clear position N' above the position list, then measure it again. The notification after clearing can undo it.
help.measure.trouble.4.fix: Stop it with 'Cancel measurement' and check in Connect & check that the measurement method is connected.
help.measure.real.1: A real run takes the channel count × the sweep length: about 1 min 30 s per position for 7.1.4 at 256k.
help.measure.real.2: Keep the room quiet and leave the mic alone during the sweeps.
help.measure.real.3: Without REW Pro, measure in REW and bring the files in with 'Import mdat'. The correction is the same as for measurements made in this app.
help.measure.real.4: The demo data is a real measurement of the demo room at its listening position only. For real use, measure 5 positions or more.
help.measure.mdat.start.2: Measure each channel in REW, save the measurements as an .mdat file, then press 'Import mdat' under Measure & import.
help.measure.mdat.s1.head: Naming measurements in REW
help.measure.mdat.s1.1: Name each measurement with the channel name and the position number.
help.measure.mdat.s1.2: For position 1, use the channel name only. Example: L, SW1
help.measure.mdat.s1.3: From position 2, add _P2, _P3 to the name. Example: L_P2
help.measure.mdat.s2.head: The window that opens after picking a file
help.measure.mdat.s2.1: Each row shows a measurement name from REW.
help.measure.mdat.s2.2: The channel and position recognized from the name are filled in.
help.measure.mdat.s2.3: Each row says whether the measurement is unreadable, bass only (looks like a sub) or full range.
help.measure.mdat.s2.4: Names that are not recognized are set to 'Skip'. Pick a channel to use them.
help.measure.mdat.s2.5: If everything is right, press 'Import measurements (N)'. A row with a problem turns this button off.
help.measure.mdat.s3.head: One file per position also works
help.measure.mdat.s3.1: Pressing 'Import mdat' twice fills positions 1 and 2 in turn.
help.measure.mdat.s3.2: 'Manage files' imports a whole file into a chosen position, or clears just that position.
help.measure.mdat.s3.3: Only the file's positions and channels are replaced; other measurements stay.
help.measure.mdat.s4.head: Channel names
help.measure.mdat.s4.1: A name without a number, such as SUB, SW or LFE, means SW1.
help.measure.mdat.s4.2: With several subs, add the number as in SW2. 'SW 2' with a space reads as position 2.
help.measure.mdat.s5.head: Names that are not recognized
help.measure.mdat.s5.2: DBA L: DBA comes before L.
help.measure.mdat.s5.4: Pick the channel for such measurements in the window.
help.measure.mdat.s6.head: Keep in mind
help.measure.mdat.s6.1: Set the timing reference to Acoustic when measuring in REW, so the time differences between channels are kept.
help.measure.mdat.s6.2: The number of positions is set under System's measurement arrangement. Higher position numbers are skipped.
help.calibrate.steps.goal: Choose a correction mode, press 'Calculate correction', then review the result on the SPL, GD, XO and BA tabs and change only what needs it. Changing a setting shows 'Recalculation needed'; the result changes only when you calculate again.
help.calibrate.steps.1.do: Choose the correction mode and press 'Calculate correction' in the step header.
help.calibrate.steps.1.see: The mode is how much latency the correction filters may add. Minimum latency corrects magnitude only; Low latency and Standard use more latency to correct the bass phase too. The first run starts with the XO recommendation; the job tray shows progress and the time left.
help.calibrate.steps.2.do: Look at the verdict card and the channel scorecard.
help.calibrate.steps.2.see: The share of 20–200 Hz within ±1 dB of the target should grow, and the 20–100 Hz GD spread should shrink. Select a channel in the scorecard to show it in the graph.
help.calibrate.steps.3.do: On the SPL tab, compare the before and after curves with the dashed target.
help.calibrate.steps.3.see: The shaded area outside is where RC does not act. Inside it, an after curve that follows the target evenly is a good correction; narrow deep dips are deliberately not filled. Drag points to edit the target; right-click empty space for the Flat, Harman and Cinema presets.
help.calibrate.steps.4.see: GD is how late sound arrives at each frequency. Lower bass peaks and a flatter curve are better.
help.calibrate.steps.5.do: Under RC range, set the band RC corrects and the boost limit.
help.calibrate.steps.5.see: 'Automatic upper limit' sets the limit from the room volume or room size. The boost limit caps every boost by RC, the XO PEQ and the sub bus PEQ.
help.calibrate.steps.6.do: On the XO tab, pick a channel and look at the XO and XO PEQ.
help.calibrate.steps.6.see: It draws the channel's main, sub and their sum. A good XO has a sum that follows the target without dips or bumps around the XO. Drag the vertical line to change the XO. A PEQ upper limit of 0 means XO × 4.
help.calibrate.steps.7.do: With two subs or more, look at the graph and value table on the BA tab.
help.calibrate.steps.7.see: Each color is one sub; dashed is before alignment, solid after, and the thick line is the sub sum. A flat sum without dips and small sub sum flatness and seat spread figures are better. The table lists each sub's gain, delay, polarity and all-pass to enter in the DSP.
help.calibrate.steps.8.do: Under Bass alignment (BA), set the infra sub and each sub's method.
help.calibrate.steps.8.see: Choosing an infra sub puts an LP on it and the matching HP on the other subs. Automatic finds the values by calculation, Fixed uses the values as entered, and a bundle keeps the relative values of its subs. After a change, 'Calculate subs only' recalculates just the BA tab. Odd settings show a warning.
help.calibrate.steps.9.do: With 3 positions or more, you can turn on 'Use MIMO' and press 'Calculate MIMO'.
help.calibrate.steps.9.see: Support filters are IIR by default (PEQ 9 + all-pass 3) and take a few minutes. 'Calculate supports as FIR' uses an 8,000-tap FIR per support: about a minute and shorter bass ringing, but many FIR taps, which suits PC DSPs such as CamillaDSP. When it ends, the SPL tab draws the MIMO applied curve.
help.calibrate.checks.1: Changing a setting such as the mode, range, target, XO or sub values shows 'Recalculation needed'. Nothing is recalculated automatically.
help.calibrate.checks.2: 'Take result values' copies the last result's sub gain, delay, polarity and all-pass into the fields without calculating. A 'Calculate subs only' result shows on the BA tab only; calculate the correction again to export it.
help.calibrate.checks.3: Bundled subs keep the gain, delay, polarity and all-pass you entered relative to each other; the calculation sets only the bundle's common gain, delay and polarity.
help.calibrate.checks.4: The XO recommendation calculates the full correction for each candidate (60, 80, 100, 120 Hz), takes the best value per group and calculates again. It takes a few minutes.
help.calibrate.checks.5: MIMO is a separate, heavy calculation that shortens bass ringing. Calculating the correction again keeps the MIMO result but marks it 'Recalculation needed'.
help.calibrate.checks.6: The ultra latency mode (30–200 ms) can be chosen only with 'Show expert options' on in Settings.
help.calibrate.trouble.1.symptom: 'There are no measured positions to calculate from' appears.
help.calibrate.trouble.1.fix: Measure, or import mdat files, in Measure & import.
help.calibrate.trouble.2.fix: It needs 3 measured positions or more, 'Use MIMO' turned on, and a correction result.
help.calibrate.trouble.3.fix: 'Cancel' in the job tray stops it. Standard mode, the XO recommendation and MIMO (IIR) take long. MIMO is much faster with 'Calculate supports as FIR' on.
help.calibrate.trouble.4.fix: 'Almost no passband is left' means the sub's LP is below twice its HP, so it plays almost nothing; check the fixed filters for an LP on a sub that is not the infra sub. 'Gain … is too high' means a sub gain above +12 dB, possibly filling a blocked band with gain. Fix the filters and check again with 'Calculate subs only'.
help.calibrate.real.1: More positions and channels take longer to calculate. The job tray shows the time left.
help.calibrate.real.2: BA searches each sub's polarity and delay within ±12 ms of its arrival and weighs the summing efficiency, how well the subs add up, along with flatness. Less cancellation gives more maximum bass level from the same amplifiers.
help.calibrate.real.3: Graphs and figures are calculated. Measure again after loading the DSP to confirm.
help.export.steps.goal: Export the correction as a CamillaDSP configuration and as a REW mdat file that compares before and after.
help.export.steps.1.do: See what will be exported under 'Correction to export'.
help.export.steps.1.see: It shows the correction mode, total latency, channels, the RC range and whether MIMO is included.
help.export.steps.2.do: Press 'Export CamillaDSP configuration' in the step header.
help.export.steps.2.see: The export folder's camilladsp folder receives the configuration (secs_<mode>.yml in configs) and 48 kHz FIR wav files (in coeffs). It has the CamillaDSP folder layout, so it can be copied as it is. The configuration holds the input PEQ and FIR, the bass management XO, the sub bus gain, delay, polarity and PEQ, and the LFE (+10 dB, 120 Hz) to every sub; with MIMO included, the support paths too.
help.export.steps.3.see: One file, 'SECS 보정 전후 <mode>.mdat', is saved; open it with File > Open in REW. Each channel has <number>_<channel>_1 before, _2 after and _3 + MIMO. _1 is the listening position measurement as is, _2 is the calculated channel correction with the sub sum, and _3 appears only with MIMO included. Subs follow at the end, as measured.
help.export.steps.4.do: Open the saved files with 'Open folder'.
help.export.steps.4.see: By default this is the '<date> <project name>' folder under SECS_export next to the project. REW mdat goes into a SECS_mdat_RC_BA(_MIMO)_<mode>_<time> folder inside it, and the CamillaDSP configuration into camilladsp.
help.export.steps.5.do: If needed, press 'Save staged mdat' under Advanced.
help.export.steps.5.see: Each channel gets calculated responses for the main and sub before correction, the XO target, the correction after summing and MIMO applied (when included). Use it to compare in REW what each stage changed.
help.export.steps.6.do: See the 'CamillaDSP' tab for loading it into CamillaDSP.
help.export.steps.6.see: The devices in the configuration are test files (in.raw, out.raw). Change them to the loopback and the interface in the GUI. For routing, change only the numbers in route_in and route_out on the Mixers tab.
help.export.checks.1: Nothing can be exported without a correction result or while it is being calculated. Exporting a result marked 'Recalculation needed' saves the last calculated result.
help.export.checks.2: MIMO is included only when 'Use MIMO' is on, MIMO is calculated, and 3 positions or more are measured. Then the folder name gets _MIMO and the mdat gets a '+ MIMO' measurement.
help.export.checks.3: The mdat levels use the REW SPL offset from the measurement.
help.export.trouble.1.symptom: The export buttons cannot be pressed.
help.export.trouble.1.fix: Check that a correction result exists and that nothing is being calculated. The reason shows in the step header.
help.export.trouble.2.symptom: 'The export files could not be written' appears.
help.export.trouble.2.fix: Check the export folder's location and write permission, or pick another folder with 'Change…' and export again.
help.export.trouble.3.symptom: The mdat levels look wrong in REW.
help.export.trouble.3.fix: Check that the measurement in REW kept its SPL offset. Imported mdat files keep their original offset.
help.export.real.1: Load the exported configuration into CamillaDSP. Turn the amplifiers off before switching.
help.export.real.2: After applying it, measure again at the listening position and compare with the after curves in the mdat.
help.export.real.3: Every correction mode delays the sound. The total latency is under 'Correction to export' and at the top of the configuration file. For video, move the player's audio sync earlier by that much.
help.export.camilla.start.1: This is how to listen to the SECS 2R correction through CamillaDSP, from a PC with nothing installed to sound.
help.export.camilla.start.2: The order is the same on Windows and macOS. It follows CamillaDSP 4.1; screen names may differ slightly between versions.
help.export.camilla.s1.head: Four things you need
help.export.camilla.s1.1: CamillaDSP: release 4.1.3 from github.com/HEnquist/camilladsp. Just unpack it.
help.export.camilla.s1.3: Loopback: VB-CABLE (vb-audio.com) on Windows, BlackHole on macOS.
help.export.camilla.s1.4: Audio interface: the one you use now.
help.export.camilla.s2.head: Signal path
help.export.camilla.s2.1: Loopback: CamillaDSP takes the sound from here (capture device).
help.export.camilla.s2.3: Interface: CamillaDSP plays out here (playback device).
help.export.camilla.s2.4: Send the player's sound to the loopback: on Windows make CABLE Input the default playback device, on macOS set the sound output to BlackHole.
help.export.camilla.s2.5: VB-CABLE on Windows is reliable for stereo. For 12 channels such as 7.1.4, BlackHole 16ch on macOS is easier.
help.export.camilla.s3.head: Make the CamillaDSP folder first
help.export.camilla.s3.1: bin and gui: unpack the downloads here.
help.export.camilla.s3.2: configs and coeffs: create these empty folders beforehand. Without them the GUI closes right after starting.
help.export.camilla.s3.3: If your user name has non-Latin characters, create it at a Latin path such as C:\camilladsp and fix the paths in the GUI's settings file: gui\camillagui_backend\_internal\config\camillagui.yml
help.export.camilla.s4.head: Copy the exported files
help.export.camilla.s4.1: The exported camilladsp folder has the CamillaDSP folder layout. Copy the files of both folders as they are.
help.export.camilla.s4.2: The yml in configs → CamillaDSP's configs
help.export.camilla.s4.3: The wav files in coeffs → CamillaDSP's coeffs. The configuration refers to ../coeffs/, so they open as they are.
help.export.camilla.s4.4: in.raw is for SECS 2R's own checks; do not copy it.
help.export.camilla.s5.head: Starting: two windows and a browser
help.export.camilla.s5.1: Run the commands in the camilladsp folder. On Windows, type cmd into that folder's address bar.
help.export.camilla.s5.2: Keep the CamillaDSP engine window open. Closing it stops the sound.
help.export.camilla.s5.3: -g-20 starts at −20 dB volume. Turn the amplifiers down at first as well.
help.export.camilla.s5.4: On macOS, allow 'Terminal would like to access the microphone'. If denied, there is silence without an error.
help.export.camilla.s6.head: Uploading in the GUI: Files tab
help.export.camilla.s6.1: If you copied the files, just press the star next to the configuration under Configs.
help.export.camilla.s6.2: Upload all wav files from coeffs first, with Upload files under Filters.
help.export.camilla.s6.3: Then upload the yml with Upload files under Configs.
help.export.camilla.s6.4: Valid should show a green check; otherwise hover over it for the reason.
help.export.camilla.s6.5: The star makes it the active configuration and loads it into the GUI.
help.export.camilla.s6.6: Without the wav files it still shows Valid and fails when applied, so upload the wav files first.
help.export.camilla.s6.7: A file with the same name is overwritten without asking.
help.export.camilla.s7.head: Devices: the Devices tab
help.export.camilla.s7.2: Capture device is the loopback; set channels to route_in's in.
help.export.camilla.s7.3: Playback device is the interface; set channels to route_out's out.
help.export.camilla.s7.4: The two devices have different clocks, so turn on Rate adjust. On Windows set the resampler to AsyncSinc.
help.export.camilla.s7.5: Pick device names with the magnifier. The list appears only while the CamillaDSP window runs.
help.export.camilla.s7.6: On macOS set type to CoreAudio and capture to BlackHole 16ch, and leave the resampler empty.
help.export.camilla.s7.7: Leave format empty. F32_LE gives an error.
help.export.camilla.s7.8: On Windows set Sound control panel › device Properties › Advanced › Default format to 48000 Hz for both devices.
help.export.camilla.s7.9: Start chunksize at 1024; use 2048 if the sound drops out, 512 to lower latency.
help.export.camilla.s8.head: The channel order at the top of the configuration
help.export.camilla.s8.1: The comment at the top of the configuration lists the input order (what CamillaDSP receives) and the output order (what it plays out).
help.export.camilla.s8.2: Numbers start at 0: interface output 1 is 0.
help.export.camilla.s8.3: Saving from the GUI removes this comment. The same order is in the Title tab's description.
help.export.camilla.s9.head: If the player's order differs: route_in on the Mixers tab
help.export.camilla.s9.1: Most players send LFE fourth. SECS 2R's inputs have LFE last.
help.export.camilla.s9.2: Columns are the channels the player sends, numbered from 0. Move only the cells of the Ls, Rs and LFE rows.
help.export.camilla.s9.3: Pressing a cell opens a small window. Delete the connection and press + on the new cell.
help.export.camilla.s9.4: The Windows 7.1 order is FL FR FC LFE BL BR SL SR: back before side.
help.export.camilla.s10.head: If the wiring differs: route_out
help.export.camilla.s10.1: Example: the sub on interface output 4, the surrounds on 5 and 6.
help.export.camilla.s10.2: out is the interface's output count. Change the playback channels under Devices to match.
help.export.camilla.s10.3: Move only the cells of the output 4, 5 and 6 rows. CamillaDSP's numbers are one lower.
help.export.camilla.s11.head: Apply and check
help.export.camilla.s11.1: Apply to DSP sends the GUI's configuration to CamillaDSP.
help.export.camilla.s11.2: State RUNNING means it is running. The input and output meters move when the player plays.
help.export.camilla.s11.3: Play one channel at a time and check that the right speaker sounds, with a channel test file or REW's signal generator.
help.export.camilla.s11.4: If Clipped samples grows, lower the player's volume or the GUI's Volume.
help.export.camilla.s11.5: When it works, press Save to file. From then on, starting the CamillaDSP window plays with the last configuration.
help.export.camilla.s12.head: Latency: video sync
help.export.camilla.s12.1: Every correction mode delays the sound. The total latency is at the top of the configuration file and on the Title tab.
help.export.camilla.s12.2: For video, move the player's audio sync earlier by that much: −200 ms for 200 ms ultra latency.
help.export.camilla.s13.head: Common problems
help.export.camilla.s13.1: The GUI closes at once: create the configs and coeffs folders inside camilladsp.
help.export.camilla.s13.2: State Offline: the CamillaDSP window is closed or was started without -p1234.
help.export.camilla.s13.3: State STALLED: the player plays to a device other than the loopback.
help.export.camilla.s13.4: RUNNING but silent: on macOS check the microphone permission; on Windows the default playback device and 48000 Hz.
help.export.camilla.s13.5: wrong number of channels: make the device channels equal to route_in's in and route_out's out.
help.export.camilla.s13.6: unknown variant F32_LE: empty the device's format.
help.export.camilla.s13.7: Dropouts every few minutes: turn on Rate adjust; on Windows also use the AsyncSinc resampler, and raise chunksize if it continues.
help.export.camilla.s13.8: Unable to find coefficient file: check that the wav files are in coeffs.

tutorial.glossary.rew: Room EQ Wizard, a measurement program. This app can run its sweeps through REW.
tutorial.glossary.api: The connection through which this app drives REW. It needs REW Pro, and REW must start with the -api option.
tutorial.glossary.calibration: A file (.cal) that corrects the measurement mic's frequency response.
tutorial.glossary.sweep: A measurement signal that glides from low to high frequencies (a log sine).
tutorial.glossary.polarity: Whether a speaker pushes or pulls (+/−). When two speakers play the same band with opposite polarity, the bass cancels.
tutorial.glossary.dsp: The processor that runs the correction filters, such as CamillaDSP, Tesira or miniDSP.
tutorial.glossary.fir: A filter that corrects magnitude and phase together. More taps give finer low-frequency resolution.
tutorial.glossary.iir: Short filters such as parametric EQ (PEQ) bands, counted in bands.
tutorial.glossary.dbfs: Level relative to digital full scale, 0 dBFS. −20 dBFS is 20 dB below full scale.
tutorial.glossary.timing: A reference signal played with the sweep so that every channel's arrival time is measured on the same clock.
tutorial.glossary.mimo: Multi-Input Multi-Output: a correction that uses several speakers to shorten the ringing and decay of low-frequency room modes.
tutorial.glossary.mdat: REW's file for a set of measurements.
tutorial.glossary.rc: Room correction: it reduces the peaks and dips the room puts into the frequency response.
tutorial.glossary.spl: The frequency response graph. Correction draws it with the target level at 0 dB.
tutorial.glossary.target: The curve the correction aims for.
tutorial.glossary.gd: Group delay: the arrival delay at each frequency. It grows where room modes ring long.
tutorial.glossary.xo: Crossover: the frequency where mains and subs split the band.
tutorial.glossary.peq: A parametric EQ band set by frequency, gain and Q.
tutorial.glossary.boost: The most the correction may raise the level. It protects headroom and drivers.
tutorial.glossary.lp_hp: A low-pass cuts the highs; a high-pass cuts the lows.
tutorial.glossary.gain: The value (dB) that raises or lowers the level.
tutorial.glossary.delay: The value (ms) that holds a signal back on purpose, aligning each sub's arrival.
tutorial.glossary.allpass: A filter that leaves magnitude alone and turns only the phase around one frequency.
tutorial.glossary.dba: Double Bass Array: front-wall and rear-wall subs, the rear ones delayed and in opposite polarity, canceling bass reflections.
tutorial.sample.rail.title: Step rail
tutorial.sample.rail: The rail: the five steps and the state of each. A blocked step shows a lock and a short reason; open it to see what it needs.
tutorial.sample.rail.why: The steps build on each other. A step's main action turns on once the steps before it are done.
tutorial.sample.status.title: Project status
tutorial.sample.status: Project status: setup, positions, correction, measurement method and file in one place.
tutorial.sample.help.title: Open help
tutorial.sample.help.why: Each step has a walkthrough, checks and troubleshooting. Help does not block the screen, so you can follow it while working.
tutorial.sample.tray.title: Job tray
tutorial.sample.tray: The job tray: progress, cancel and history of long jobs such as measuring, calculating the correction or MIMO, and exporting.
tutorial.sample.tray.why: Long jobs never block the screen, and 'Cancel' in the job tray really stops them.
tutorial.sample.compute.title: Calculate correction
tutorial.sample.compute: Press 'Calculate correction' in the step header.
tutorial.sample.compute.why: Measuring alone changes nothing; calculating produces the filters for the DSP.
tutorial.sample.compute.busy: Calculating. Progress shows in the job tray; the tutorial moves on when it ends.

project.new.start.empty.hint: Starts with the chosen setup and no measurements.
project.new.start.sample.hint: Starts with the demo room setup (7.1.4 · 3 subs, listening position only).
project.new.fixed: The demo room's setup and sub count are fixed.
project.new.where: Choosing a location creates the project file (.secs) there right away. The export DSP starts as CamillaDSP.
project.unsaved.body_untitled: This project has never been saved.
project.unsaved.loss: Without saving, changes since the last save are lost.

project.tutorial.lead: You can walk from System to Export without a mic or REW.
project.tutorial.point.project: A separate project of the demo room (7.1.4 · 3 subs) opens.
project.tutorial.point.measure: Measuring is simulated, so nothing plays. The demo data is a real measurement of the demo room at its listening position.

project.tutorial.point.return: From the tutorial list you can hide the tutorial for now, start over or end it. Ending it returns to the current project.
project.tutorial.dirty: There are unsaved changes, so a window to choose whether to save opens first.

tutorial.q.system.presets.title: Setup presets
tutorial.q.system.presets.text: Choosing a preset fills in the speaker setup at once. Change the sub count with − / + beside it. The demo room is 7.1.4 with three subs.
tutorial.q.system.patch.title: Output patch
tutorial.q.system.patch.text: Set each speaker's measurement output, polarity and size in the output patch.
tutorial.q.system.dsp.title: Export DSP
tutorial.q.system.dsp.text: Under Export DSP, set the device that runs the filters and its FIR tap and IIR band budgets. These budgets check whether the filters fit the device.
tutorial.q.system.output.title: Fix the SW3 output
tutorial.q.system.output.text: SW3's measurement output is wrongly set to 16. Change it to 6 in the Subwoofers rows of the output patch.
tutorial.q.system.output.why: The measurement output is the audio interface output that plays the speaker's sweep. It must match the real wiring for the sweep to come out of that speaker.
tutorial.q.system.output.note: Changed SW3's measurement output to a free number.
tutorial.q.system.output.blocked: SW3 has no output. Check the setup.
tutorial.q.system.layout_next.title: Measurement arrangement
tutorial.q.system.layout_next.text: Setup and measurement arrangement share the System step. Next, review the measurement arrangement.
tutorial.q.system.layout.title: Measurement positions
tutorial.q.system.layout.text: Check the position count and the map under Measurement arrangement. Position 1 is always the listening position.
tutorial.q.system.timing.title: Timing reference
tutorial.q.system.timing.text: Set the start delay, the timing reference and the reference output.
tutorial.q.system.single.title: Main seat
tutorial.q.system.single.text: The tutorial uses the listening position only. For real measurements, use several positions, such as 'One chair', 'Sofa for 2–3' or 'Two rows'.
tutorial.q.system.single.why: More positions avoid overcorrecting for one point. MIMO needs at least 3 positions.
tutorial.q.system.next.title: Go to Connect & check
tutorial.q.system.next.text: The next step is Connect & check. Move on to it.
tutorial.q.system.next.hint: Press 'Go to Connect & check' in the step header.
tutorial.q.system.next.blocked: The setup has problems. Fix duplicate outputs or channel errors first.
tutorial.q.connect.sidebar.title: Project status
tutorial.q.connect.sidebar.text: The project status under the rail shows the setup, positions, correction, measurement method and file. Save from the project menu; press 'Help' to open help.
tutorial.q.connect.rail.title: Step rail
tutorial.q.connect.rail.text: The step rail on the left shows the current step and opens the others. The magenta accent means the tutorial is on. A dashed outline marks something to look at; a solid outline marks something to press.
tutorial.q.connect.connection.title: Measurement method
tutorial.q.connect.connection.text: Under Measurement method, choose built-in measurement, REW, simulated measurement or 'Import mdat files only'. With REW, the app checks the API connection to REW Pro. Without Pro, import mdat files instead.
tutorial.q.connect.audio.title: Mic and audio
tutorial.q.connect.audio.text: With built-in measurement or REW, you set the input device, input channel and sweep length. With REW, also check the mic calibration file. The tutorial uses simulated measurement and opens no real device.
tutorial.q.connect.retry.title: Choose simulated measurement
tutorial.q.connect.retry.text: Choose simulated measurement under Measurement method. Nothing plays through the speakers.
tutorial.q.connect.retry.why: A measurement method must be set before measuring. Real measuring with REW needs REW Pro in API mode. The tutorial uses silent simulated measurement.
tutorial.q.connect.retry.blocked: Simulated measurement is unavailable. Check the status under Measurement method.
tutorial.q.connect.level_next.title: Level check
tutorial.q.connect.level_next.text: Device connection and the level check share this step. Next, check the channel levels.
tutorial.q.connect.master.title: Master output
tutorial.q.connect.master.text: Master output sets how loud the level check plays. 'Check all channel levels' plays the channels in turn.
tutorial.q.connect.levels.title: Channel level check
tutorial.q.connect.levels.text: Press 'Check all channel levels'. You can also fill in the levels with 'Fill with defaults'.
tutorial.q.connect.levels.why: Too low and the input is buried in noise; too high and it clips. Each channel plays pink noise to check that the mic input lands in the recommended range (−30…−15 dBFS). The tutorial has no real mic, so the mic meter stays empty and the channel values are filled in as examples.
tutorial.q.connect.levels.note: Filled in a default level for every channel.
tutorial.q.connect.levels.busy: Playing the channels in turn. The tutorial moves on once every level is recorded.
tutorial.q.connect.levels.hint: Press 'Check all channel levels' in the step header.
tutorial.q.connect.next.title: Go to Measure & import
tutorial.q.connect.next.text: With the levels checked, move on to Measure & import.
tutorial.q.connect.next.blocked: Choose a measurement method and wait for playback to finish.
tutorial.q.measure.positions.title: Position list
tutorial.q.measure.positions.text: Choose the position to measure in the position list. A position is marked 'Measured' once all its channels are measured.
tutorial.q.measure.sample.title: Demo data
tutorial.q.measure.sample.text: Press 'Load demo data' to load the listening position's measurements.
tutorial.q.measure.sample.why: The correction is calculated from measured responses. In real use, 'Measure this position' sweeps every channel. The demo data is a real measurement of the demo room (7.1.4 · 3 subs) at the listening position.
tutorial.q.measure.sample.note: Loaded the demo room's position 1 measurements.
tutorial.q.measure.sample.blocked: Demo data loads only in the tutorial project. Wait for other device jobs to finish.
tutorial.q.measure.graph.title: Measurement graph
tutorial.q.measure.graph.text: The graph shows the frequency response of each channel. With several positions measured, the bold line is the listening position.
tutorial.q.measure.mdat.title: Import REW mdat
tutorial.q.measure.mdat.text: You can import an mdat file of REW measurements named L, R, SW1 and so on. From position 2, use names such as L_P2. The 'mdat import' tab in Help has the details.
tutorial.q.measure.next.title: Go to Correction
tutorial.q.measure.next.text: The measurements are ready. Move on to Correction.
tutorial.q.measure.next.blocked: Load measurements first, and wait for device jobs to finish.
tutorial.q.calibrate.mode.title: Correction mode
tutorial.q.calibrate.mode.text: 'Calculate correction' turns the measurements into filters. The mode limits the latency the filters may add. Minimum latency corrects magnitude only; Low latency and Standard also correct the bass phase.
tutorial.q.calibrate.graph.title: Result graph
tutorial.q.calibrate.graph.text: Before calculating, the SPL tab shows the measurement and the target. After calculating, you can compare the corrected response and the GD and XO curves.
tutorial.q.calibrate.tabs.title: Graphs and settings
tutorial.q.calibrate.tabs.text: The graph tabs are SPL, GD and XO. The correction settings are below, in the RC range, crossover and bass alignment sections.
tutorial.q.calibrate.compute.title: Calculate correction
tutorial.q.calibrate.compute.text: Press 'Calculate correction' to make the filters for the DSP.
tutorial.q.calibrate.compute.why: Measuring alone does not change the sound. The calculation makes the RC and BA filters. Progress shows in the job tray, where you can also cancel.
tutorial.q.calibrate.compute.busy: Calculating the correction. Progress shows in the job tray.
tutorial.q.calibrate.compute.hint: Press 'Calculate correction' in the step header.
tutorial.q.calibrate.compute.blocked: Check the measurements and the sub setup, and wait for running jobs to finish.
tutorial.q.calibrate.spl.title: SPL response
tutorial.q.calibrate.spl.text: The SPL tab draws the before and after curves over the dashed target. The shaded area outside is the band RC leaves alone. Inside it, a good correction has the after curve following the target evenly. Narrow, deep dips are deliberately not filled all the way.
tutorial.q.calibrate.metrics.title: Result figures
tutorial.q.calibrate.metrics.text: On the verdict card, a higher 'Within ±1 dB' is better. A smaller 'GD spread' means a more even arrival across frequencies. 'Total latency' is the time the filters add. See the filter counts in the channel scorecard and below the graph.
tutorial.q.calibrate.gd.title: Group delay
tutorial.q.calibrate.gd.text: The GD tab shows how late each frequency arrives, in ms. Bass peaks are room modes that keep ringing. Within the RC range, the lower the peaks and the flatter the curve after correction, the better.
tutorial.q.calibrate.xo_open.title: Open the XO tab
tutorial.q.calibrate.xo_open.text: Open the XO tab to see how the main and sub responses join.
tutorial.q.calibrate.xo_open.why: Mains and subs must sum in phase around the XO, or cancellation leaves a dip or a hump. This tab sets the XO and XO PEQ for each channel group.
tutorial.q.calibrate.xo_open.note: Opened the XO tab. The curves appear when the calculation is done.
tutorial.q.calibrate.xo_open.hint: Press the XO tab of the graph.
tutorial.q.calibrate.xo_open.blocked: Check the measurements and the sub setup, and wait for running jobs to finish.
tutorial.q.calibrate.xo.title: Crossover
tutorial.q.calibrate.xo.text: The XO tab draws the chosen channel's main, sub and their sum over the target. A good XO has the sum following the target with no dip or bump around the XO. Drag the vertical line, or change the frequency in the crossover section. 'Recommend XO' calculates every candidate in full and picks the best value per group.
tutorial.q.calibrate.ba_open.title: Open the BA tab
tutorial.q.calibrate.ba_open.text: Open the BA tab to see how the subs are aligned.
tutorial.q.calibrate.ba_open.why: Several subs reinforce or cancel each other differently at each seat. BA (bass alignment) finds values for each sub so the sub sum is even and the subs add up instead of canceling. That is why this tab appears only with two or more subs.
tutorial.q.calibrate.ba_open.hint: Press the BA tab of the graph.
tutorial.q.calibrate.ba_open.blocked: Check the measurements and the sub setup, and wait for running jobs to finish.
tutorial.q.calibrate.ba_graph.title: Sub sum graph
tutorial.q.calibrate.ba_graph.text: The BA graph draws each sub in its own color. Dashed lines are before alignment; solid lines are after. A good sub sum follows the target without deep dips. The legend names each line.
tutorial.q.calibrate.ba_metrics.title: BA result figures
tutorial.q.calibrate.ba_metrics.text: In the result line, 'Sub sum flatness' is how much the sub sum ripples, so smaller after alignment is better. 'Seat spread' is the difference between measurement positions. The value table lists each sub's gain, delay, polarity and all-pass for the DSP; each sub name has its curve's color.
tutorial.q.calibrate.ba_metrics.why: BA aims at these two numbers: an even sub sum at the listening position and a small difference between seats. The tutorial demo has one position, so the seat spread is empty.
tutorial.q.calibrate.ba_settings.title: Alignment method per sub
tutorial.q.calibrate.ba_settings.text: Choose an alignment method for each sub. Automatic finds the gain, delay and polarity by calculation; Fixed uses the values you entered. A bundle keeps the relative values of its subs while fitting the common values. Under Advanced, choose the sub to edit and its detailed values.
tutorial.q.calibrate.ba_settings.why: Keep the values of subs already matched by their layout, such as a DBA, with Fixed or a bundle, and leave the rest on Automatic. 'Take result values' copies the last calculated values into the fields as a starting point for Fixed.
tutorial.q.calibrate.infra.title: Infra sub
tutorial.q.calibrate.infra.text: Set the infra sub to SW3. In the demo room, SW3 plays the deepest bass.
tutorial.q.calibrate.infra.why: The infra sub plays only the deepest band and the other subs the band above. The infra sub gets an LP and the other subs the matching HP automatically, and the infra band level is matched to the band above.
tutorial.q.calibrate.infra.note: Set the last sub as the infra sub (25 Hz, LR24).
tutorial.q.calibrate.infra.blocked: At least two subs are needed. If a calculation is running, wait for it to finish.
tutorial.q.calibrate.ba_filters.title: Fixed filters
tutorial.q.calibrate.ba_filters.text: Fixed filters (HP, LP, PEQ) always apply to this sub's output. Choosing an infra sub adds an LP on it and an HP on the other subs at the infra XO frequency. Whatever the method, the alignment is calculated with these filters in place.
tutorial.q.calibrate.subs.title: Calculate subs only
tutorial.q.calibrate.subs.text: The settings changed. Press 'Calculate subs only' to recalculate the BA result.
tutorial.q.calibrate.subs.why: Changing a setting leaves the result out of date. 'Calculate subs only' recalculates just the BA and redraws this tab's graph and table. It takes a few seconds.
tutorial.q.calibrate.subs.busy: Recalculating the BA. The graph and table change when it ends.
tutorial.q.calibrate.subs.hint: Press 'Calculate subs only' in the bass alignment section.
tutorial.q.calibrate.subs.blocked: Check the measurements and the sub setup, and wait for running jobs to finish.
tutorial.q.calibrate.ba_after.title: Updated BA result
tutorial.q.calibrate.ba_after.text: After 'Calculate subs only', the infra sub plays only below the infra XO and the other subs only above it, so the sub sum joins the two. The value table shows the newly found values. This result shows only on the BA tab; to use it on the SPL and XO tabs and in the export, press 'Calculate correction' again.
tutorial.q.calibrate.next.title: Go to Export
tutorial.q.calibrate.next.text: Move on to Export. A 'Calculate subs only' result is not part of the full correction result. To include it, press 'Calculate correction' again.
tutorial.q.calibrate.next.blocked: Check the measurements and the sub setup, and wait for running jobs to finish.
tutorial.q.export.mdat.title: REW mdat
tutorial.q.export.mdat.text: 'Save REW mdat' writes measurements named per channel: _1 before, _2 after and _3 + MIMO. _2 and _3 are calculated predictions.
tutorial.q.export.camilla.title: CamillaDSP
tutorial.q.export.camilla.text: 'Export CamillaDSP configuration' writes a yml configuration named after the mode and a 48 kHz FIR wav file per channel. The tutorial saves no files.
